# Client Health Score Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Client Health Score Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 20 captured build checkpoints; 5 skills; 2 knowledge files; 5 acceptance checks; 5 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; use `cli-copilot` authoring and keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review policies for uploaded portfolio files, proposed CRM, Teams and Outlook access, and the intended channel; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for Dynamics 365, Microsoft Teams and Outlook with least-privilege identities. The workshop needs no customer connection. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare client-success, account-manager, client-experience and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; do not publish the workshop to share it. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Approval ownership | Name the account owners who approve plans before client outreach; keep real client and contact data out of the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Client success leadership

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** How relationship, delivery, financial and satisfaction signals are reviewed to find at-risk clients. Manual reviews can surface risk late, overstate a score and leave retention plans without clear ownership.

Fill your baseline record:

| Client segment | Measurement period | Signals reviewed | How risk was surfaced | Retention plan owner | Approval route |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree client-health replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Client success leadership

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Client success leadership | Approve portfolio-review scope, production seams and success measures; never treat synthetic scores or indicators as predictions. |
| Account owners | Review every retention plan before any client outreach and own the next engagement decision. |
| Sponsor, delivery, legal and commercial reviewers | Review executive engagement, remediation and commercial proposals where applicable. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and five skills; remove web search, add no tools and record the owned agent's Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any account-data connection is approved. |
| Account data connection owners | Approve Dynamics 365, Microsoft Teams and Outlook access with least-privilege identities; own connection failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check CHS-01 through CHS-05, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject reshoot-required frames and uncited answers. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route client decisions to account owners. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Planned client-health replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed.
- [ ] The client-success owner records where relationship, delivery, financial and satisfaction signals live and how risk is reviewed today.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/client-health-score/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved and recorded before any build starts.
- [ ] The customer approves the authenticated staff audience and least-privilege scopes for client and contact data.
- [ ] The environment's data policies for knowledge sources, connectors, skills and channels are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/client-health-score/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/client-health-score/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/client-health-score/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/client-health-score/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Client Health Score Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_client-health-retention-playbook.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_client-health-synthetic-portfolio.md
8. Add skill: at-risk-clients
9. Add skill: engagement-analysis
10. Add skill: health-dashboard
11. Add skill: retention-plan
12. Add skill: satisfaction-trend
13. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
14. Open a fresh Preview conversation
15. Pass CHS-01: Client Success Leader
16. Pass CHS-02: Account Manager
17. Pass CHS-03: Client Experience Director
18. Pass CHS-04: Client Success Leader
19. Pass CHS-05: Account Manager
20. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: CHS-01, CHS-02, CHS-03, CHS-04, CHS-05. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `ClientHealthScoreAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, five skills and the confirmed model; web search is removed and no tools exist.
- [ ] The engagement and playbook cases return only their reviewed locked responses.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full final response; an annotated image is only a learner checkpoint.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before accessing client, contact or satisfaction information. Request only the scopes necessary for approved account sources. Restrict the account-team audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Schedule nothing; present the meeting as a proposal for internal review and account-owner approval. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, message or record change succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any team message or task workflow behind account-owner approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Schedule nothing; present the meeting as a proposal for internal review and account-owner approval. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, message or record change succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Outlook

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

1. **Bind Outlook — write:** Keep proposals internal; gate any email or calendar workflow behind account-owner approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Outlook:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Outlook:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Outlook:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Query no CRM, email or calendar system; use only the frozen synthetic snapshot. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, message or record change succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Account data connection owners

Replace synthetic inputs with approved Dynamics 365, Microsoft Teams and Outlook connections that preserve the reviewed input and output contract.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] After approved connections are added, replaying the locked synthetic cases confirms that no external side effect occurred.
- [ ] No live lookup, message or record change is claimed unless an approved tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Run adapted evaluations under an approved authenticated test profile so the agent's tools and connections are fully testable.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The client-success owner sets acceptance thresholds on customer data; synthetic scores, indicators and values are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; exact assertions stay separate from General quality scoring.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked client-health corpus | All five cases, CHS-01 through CHS-05, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, five skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Relationship action boundary | Any meeting, message, concession, renewal change, CRM update or certain churn prediction is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reuse only frames with a positive expected-state anchor; reshoot-required frames stay withheld. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Client success leadership

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Client success leadership

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved account-team audience and channels are selected, and the agent is tested in Preview before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review portfolio session transcripts, failed turns, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Pull before editing, push reviewed changes, then package the workspace with `pac copilot pack` for solution import.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, certainty or causal claims, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
